title: fix(update): report health check timeouts accurately
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading update failure reports when Doctor lint reaches its deadline or automatic repair cannot start an inference turn.

Related: #152759, #151546, #153049. Thanks to @Lendersmark for the detailed Linux timing analysis and elimination of competing causes.

## User Impact

Future updaters distinguish a complete lint report followed by a process/pipe stall from checks that have not produced a report. Unavailable automatic repair is recorded as skipped, preserving the original failed check as the cause. Real lint findings and failed validation remain authoritative.

This is a diagnostic fix. It cannot patch the installed 2026.9.4 updater, and it does not claim to fix an identified leaked handle on the reporter's host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The published 2026.9.4 driver shares one 300-second budget across snapshot preparation and all candidate checks. Its final elapsed-time suffix measures the entire rehearsal, while each step has its own duration. The cited 299-second total and 22–40-second lint duration are consistent with lint starting about 259–277 seconds into that window. The driver also copies the aggregate log tail into the failed step: `Doctor complete.` belongs to ordinary repair and is not lint's terminal JSON. Those artifact fields alone therefore do not establish that lint completed before termination. Published 2026.9.5 already invokes the shared one-shot exit helper after lint.

The canary owner now freezes same-child report and process-exit evidence before teardown, keeps explicit timeout metadata, and distinguishes open output pipes from a process that has not exited. It reports a kill only when signal and cleanup evidence support it. Existing lint findings retain their full capped budget; process context uses the existing diagnostic tail. The repair owner records inference unavailability before any turn as skipped. This complements #153147, whose scope excludes repair-path implementation.

## Evidence

- Regression tests failed before the diagnostic fixes. The review regression also demonstrated that inserting synthetic timeout context could displace the fifth real finding; the final implementation preserves all five.
- Final canary suites: 71/71 passed across `update-candidate-canary.test.ts` and `update-candidate-canary.cleanup.test.ts`. Repair-worker boundary suite: 9/9 passed; its inputs were unchanged by the final canary correction.
- Fresh P1 autoreview: scoped-clean after resolving the finding-preservation issue.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: exit 0, including core and all core-test typechecks, changed-file lint, export scans, and source guards. `git diff --check` passed. No baseline or suppression changes.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m2y2xfndvss6zqtez7e7fr99`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35478475291): published 9.5 on Linux 6.6.141, 17 agents, 102 imported sessions (3,366 transcript events), three providers, dead local endpoints, and legacy auth-profile backup residue. Piped lint, systemd environment variables, PTY, package compile-cache entry, and Node 24.18/24.19 variants all exited normally in 6.6–7.9 seconds; config validation took 0.7–0.8 seconds. The shipped snapshot → repair → lint capture recipe also exited successfully.
- Actual published-driver cell: isolated npm 2026.9.4 → 2026.9.5, `update --tag 2026.9.5 --yes --no-restart --json`, 3.0 GiB source tree. Exit 0, `status: ok`, persisted run `succeeded`, total 99.693 s. Candidate repair 11.731 s; lint 6.026 s; config validation 0.853 s; plugin resolution 0.834 s; recovery contract 0.584 s; canary Gateway 12.889 s. Validation phase 56.824 s. No operator Gateway or state was used.

No post-completion hang was reproduced, so no leaked-resource owner or active-resource dump is claimed. The initial matrix used synthetic session data rather than the reporter's complete state; the full released-driver cell expands the source tree to 3.0 GiB with inert media padding. This does not reproduce Fedora 44 or the reporter's exact configuration.

Production delta: +48/−9 lines (net +39). Tests: +155/−0. Documentation: +15/−0.

## ClawSweeper review disposition

The exact-head review found no actionable correctness or security findings. Its sole before-merge / Rank-up item, “Add data-model compatibility proof,” is addressed by the existing contract and boundary evidence: `UPDATE_RUN_STEP_STATUSES` already includes `skipped`, the repair-attempt schema already accepts `skipped`, and the report reader selects failed steps separately. This patch changes which existing value is recorded only when repair is unavailable before any turn starts; it adds no fields, schema version, database migration, or backfill. Existing records remain valid. The repair-worker regression reads the persisted run and verifies both “Repair 1: skipped” and preservation of the original failed health check; the recorded suite passed 9/9. A new migration is therefore not applicable.

The published 2026.9.4 → 2026.9.5 cell above is upgrade-investigation evidence, not after-fix execution of the new timeout branches. Those branches are covered by the recorded 71/71 canary tests. No live post-completion hang or reporter-specific state reproduction is claimed. The campaign Codex review is scoped-clean; no semantic changes were made for landing.
